Endpoint coordinates for slice categories

The proof describing functors into a slice changes from a defining endpoint pullback to a cylinder description. Here are the coordinate calculations used in that change. Assume the Chapter 1 structures, including functor categories and pullbacks, and the walking morphism. All constructions in this note are absolute.

Write \(\chi _{X,Y,C}\colon \Fun (X,\Fun (Y,C))\iso \Fun (X\times Y,C)\) for the exponential comparison, and \(u^*\) for precomposition by \(u\). For \(\psi \colon Y\to C\), use the direct absolute slice: the pullback of endpoint evaluation \[ \Fun ([1]\times Y,C)\longrightarrow \Fun (Y,C)\times \Fun (Y,C) \] along \(C\to \Fun (Y,C)^2\), \(c\mapsto (\operatorname {const}_c,\psi )\). This is the absolute slice implementation linked below. Its comparison with the separately chosen relative slice over \(\star \) is not exported by these declarations.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For \(u\colon Y\to Z\) there is an identification of functors \[ \chi _{X,Y,C}\,\Fun (X,u^*) = (\operatorname {id}_X\times u)^*\,\chi _{X,Z,C}. \]

Proof idea

Uncurry both sides. Each becomes double evaluation after a change of product coordinates. Compare the two reassociation routes by their three projections: the first two coordinates are unchanged and the last is postcomposed with \(u\). The exponential reflection rule gives the claimed identification. In particular this applies to either endpoint insertion \(Y\to [1]\times Y\). □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Under \(\chi _{X,Y,C}\), postcomposition by the constant-family functor \(C\to \Fun (Y,C)\) becomes \(\operatorname {pr}_X^*\colon \Fun (X,C)\to \Fun (X\times Y,C)\). Postcomposition by the constant functor \(C\to \Fun (Y,C)\) with value \(\psi \) becomes the constant functor with value \(\psi \operatorname {pr}_Y\). These are identifications of functors on \(\Fun (X,C)\).

Proof idea

Double evaluation of the first construction forgets the \(Y\) coordinate and evaluates the variable functor at \(X\). Double evaluation of the second forgets the variable functor and the \(X\) coordinate and evaluates \(\psi \) at \(Y\). The product-projection and constant-family computation laws identify these maps with the uncurrying of the two asserted functors. Reflect through the exponential equivalence. □

Supplementary Lemma 3. The equivalence \[ r\colon X\times ([1]\times Y)\iso (X\times Y)\times [1] \] given by symmetry and reassociation preserves endpoint insertion: \[ r\bigl (\operatorname {id}_X\times (e,\operatorname {id}_Y)\bigr ) = (\operatorname {id}_{X\times Y},e). \] There is also a comparison for the chosen inverse of \(r\) with the insertion on the left.

Proof idea

Compute the \(X,Y,[1]\) projections. The first two are the projections of \(X\times Y\); the third is the constant endpoint \(e\). Pair their comparisons to obtain the displayed identification. For the inverse comparison, compose with \(r\), use its retraction comparison, and reflect through the equivalence \(r\). □

Supplementary Corollary 4. Put \(A=\Fun (X,C)\), \(Z=\Fun (X\times Y,C)\) and \(W=\Fun ((X\times Y)\times [1],C)\). There is a pullback square with corners \[ \begin {matrix} \Fun (X,C_{/\psi })&\longrightarrow&W \\ \big \downarrow&& \big \downarrow \\ A&\longrightarrow&Z \times Z, \end {matrix} \] where the right map is endpoint restriction, the lower map sends \(f\) to \((f\operatorname {pr}_X,\psi \operatorname {pr}_Y)\), and the left map is postcomposition with the slice projection. Its commutativity identification is the one transported from the defining slice square by the preceding comparisons.

Proof idea

Apply \(\Fun (X,-)\) to the defining slice pullback. It remains a pullback. Use the exponential and product comparisons on its corners. Supplementary Lemmas 1 and 3 identify the upper cospan map with endpoint restriction; Supplementary Lemma 2 identifies the lower one with the displayed pair. These computations give a comparison of cospans, including its specified squares. Transport the cone through that comparison. Pullback invariance supplies the assertion with the transported matching.

The lower map factors through \(\Fun (X,C)\times \Fun (Y,C)\) by \(f\mapsto (f,\psi )\). With the mapping-out join axiom, nesting the two pullbacks and using the mapping-out description of the join gives the square in the book. The coordinate calculation above is what makes that nesting apply to the specified slice diagram. □
